title: Write public notes in your own voice
statement: As a product manager, I can write a release's public notes as a piece of writing, as playful as we like, so users hear why the release matters and not a list of tickets.
overview: Trevor's example: "Unleash the Kraken!", more a blog post about why you're cool than a list of changes. The original direction was that every note links a story; prose this free does not break into notes that could each carry one, so the stories are named beside the text, and `release status` lists any delivered story that no note mentions.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A release has at most one set of public notes: Markdown with no required structure, length or tone.
A release's page shows its public and internal notes apart, each labelled.
Public notes can name the stories they talk about, as links kept apart from the text, so the writing itself need carry none.
The reader and `release guide` say that internal means for the team and not secret: anyone who can read the repository can read internal notes.
